description:
Programme or Project Overview

Lund University invites applications for a doctoral student position on risk and safety of heterogeneous swarm systems, hosted by the CHASS competence centre and funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research (SSF). Swarm systems - large numbers of cooperating drones, robots and autonomous agents - promise major advances in logistics, inspection and rescue, but their heterogeneous, dynamic composition creates new safety and assurance challenges. The doctoral project develops methods to model, analyse and certify risk in such systems.

The candidate joins a centre that brings together academia, industry and public agencies around connected autonomous systems, with access to testbeds, industrial partners and an international research network. The employment is a salaried four-year doctoral position under the Swedish collective agreement, based in Lund's engineering research environment with seminar and training support across robotics, control and software engineering.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in robotics, electrical engineering, computer science, mechanical engineering or a related field, with strong analytical and programming skills. Background in formal methods, control systems, machine learning or safety engineering is an advantage. Applications are submitted through Lund University's Varbi portal with CV, transcripts, references and a statement of interest; the closing date is 5 November 2026.

Highlights

  • PhD on risk and safety of heterogeneous swarm systems
  • SSF-funded CHASS competence centre environment
  • Modelling, assurance and certification of autonomy
  • Industry and public-agency collaboration and testbeds
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • Closing date: 5 November 2026

Doctoral students are salaried employees under Swedish collective agreements, and postdoctoral fellowships are advertised through the university's Varbi recruitment portal. The university ranks among the top 100 research universities worldwide in major rankings.
